mainTopic: נחום איש גם זו's gift, the sin of דור הפלגה, and the wickedness of אנשי סדום
overview: This amud opens by finishing the story of נחום איש גם זו. Thieves swapped the gift for the emperor with dirt, but אליהו convinced the Romans it was the miraculous dirt of אברהם אבינו. נחום was rewarded with gold, and the thieves who tried to copy him were executed. The גמרא then asks what sin דור הפלגה committed. רבי שילא's school says they wanted to hack open the sky, but scholars in ארץ ישראל mock this answer. רבי ירמיה בר אלעזר says they split into three groups with three plans, while רבי נתן says they all meant to serve עבודה זרה. Statements follow about the fate of the tower and how its area makes people forget Torah. Next the גמרא turns to אנשי סדום: פסוקים are explained to describe their sins, their arrogance from great wealth, and their cruel tricks for robbing rich people. It tells of רבי יוסי, whose lecture on these tricks was copied by thieves in ציפורי. The amud ends with סדום's unfair herding rule and an orphan who killed the oxen he was given. His reply comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Choosing נחום איש גם זו as the messenger
steps.stepSummary: The Jews pick נחום איש גם זו to carry their gift to the emperor because miracles often happen to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom should we send? We will send it with נחום איש גם זו, because he is used to miracles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing a story from the previous daf about a gift the Jews had to send to the Roman emperor. Here they decide who should bring it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing a gift to the emperor was dangerous, so they wanted a messenger who could be protected. They chose נחום because he was known for having miracles happen to him. This sets up the rest of the story, where a miracle saves him.

keyTerms.meaning: נחום איש גם זו, a תנא famous for saying 'this too is for the good'
Used to miracles; miracles often happen to him

phrases.english: Whom shall we send?

phrases.aramaic: נְשַׁדַּר בַּהֲדֵי נַחוּם אִישׁ גַּם זוֹ,
phrases.english: We will send it with Nachum of Gam Zo,
for he is experienced in miracles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a story that began on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נחום איש גם זו is chosen as the messenger because miracles often happen to him.

steps.title: The gift is stolen and replaced with dirt
steps.stepSummary: Thieves at an inn swap the treasure for dirt. The emperor feels mocked and orders נחום to be killed, but נחום says 'this too is for the good.'
steps.simpleTranslation: When he got to a certain inn, he wanted to sleep there. The people there asked him what he was carrying. He said he was bringing tax money to the emperor. At night they opened his chest, took everything, and filled it with dirt. When he arrived in Rome, they found dirt. The emperor said, 'The Jews are making fun of me!' They took נחום out to kill him. He said, 'This too is for the good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward: the treasure is stolen, the emperor is insulted, and נחום is about to be killed. Even so, נחום says this too is for the good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything seems to go wrong. נחום told the innkeepers the truth about his cargo, and that is how they knew to rob him. His calm saying, 'גם זו לטובה', sets up the miracle that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Head tax, tribute paid to the ruler
This too is for the good

phrases.english: When he reached a certain lodging,
he wanted to spend the night there.
They said to him: What do you have with you?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: קָא מוֹבֵילְנָא כְּרָגָא לְקֵיסָר.
phrases.english: He said to them: I am bringing the tax to the emperor.
They got up at night and opened his chest,
and took everything that was in it,
and filled it with dirt.
When he arrived there, dirt was found.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: אַחוֹכֵי קָא מְחַיְּיכִי בִּי יְהוּדָאֵי.
phrases.english: He said: The Jews are mocking me.
phrases.notes: The one speaking here is the emperor.

phrases.english: They took him out to kill him.
He said: This too is for the good.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the journey of the messenger chosen in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even facing death, נחום accepts what happens with 'this too is for the good.'

steps.title: אליהו suggests the dirt is אברהם's miraculous dirt
steps.stepSummary: אליהו appears in disguise and suggests the dirt may be the dirt of אברהם אבינו, which turned into weapons. They test it, and it is true.
steps.simpleTranslation: אליהו came and appeared to them as one of them. He said: Maybe this dirt is from the dirt of אברהם אבינו. When he threw dirt, it became swords, and when he threw straw, it became arrows. They checked and found it was so.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the miracle that saves נחום. אליהו gives the Romans a reason to think the dirt is a special gift, and the test proves him right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'insulting' gift is now seen as a treasure. This shows why נחום was right to say 'this too is for the good': the dirt turns out to be worth more than the stolen money.

keyTerms.meaning: אליהו הנביא, who often appears in disguise to help people
He appeared as, he looked like

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא אֵלִיָּהוּ וְאִידְּמִי לְהוּ כְּחַד מִינַּיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: Eliyahu came and appeared to them as one of them.
He said to them: Perhaps this dirt
is from the dirt of Avraham our father,
who would throw dirt and it became swords,
straw, and it became arrows.
They checked and found that it was so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא אֵלִיָּהוּ וְאִידְּמִי לְהוּ כְּחַד מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the danger of step 2 with a miracle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dirt is shown to be the miraculous dirt of אברהם אבינו.

steps.title: The dirt wins a battle and נחום is rewarded
steps.stepSummary: The Romans use the dirt to conquer a province they could not take before. They reward נחום by letting him fill his chest with gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a province they could not conquer. They threw some of that dirt on it and conquered it. They brought נחום into the treasury and said, 'Take whatever you like.' He filled his chest with gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The dirt really works in battle, and נחום is rewarded. He leaves with a chest full of gold instead of being killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story turns around completely. The stolen treasure is replaced by an even bigger reward. 'גם זו לטובה' has come true.

phrases.english: There was a province

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא הֲווֹ קָא יָכְלִי לֵיהּ לְמִיכְבְּשֵׁיהּ.
phrases.english: that they were not able to conquer.
They threw some of that dirt on it and conquered it.
They brought him into the treasury,
and said: Take whatever you like.
He filled his chest with gold.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה מָחוֹזָא דְּלָא הֲווֹ קָא יָכְלִי לֵיהּ לְמִיכְבְּשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of the discovery in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dirt conquers the province, and נחום is rewarded with gold.

steps.title: The thieves try to copy נחום and are executed
steps.stepSummary: On his way home, the innkeepers ask what he brought. נחום truthfully says he brought what he took from there. They bring dirt to the emperor, and they are executed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came back, those innkeepers asked him: What did you bring to the king's palace? He said to them: What I took from here, I brought there. They took dirt and brought it there, and the innkeepers were killed.
steps.whatsHappening: This ends the story. The thieves think their dirt is magic, try to cash in, and are punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחום does not lie. The dirt really did come from their inn. The thieves wrongly think any dirt from there is special, but the miracle was only for נחום, so the thieves pay with their lives.

keyTerms.meaning: Residents, the people of the inn

steps.whatToRemember: The story of נחום איש גם זו teaches that something that looks like a disaster can turn out for the good. The ones who tried to harm him ended up harming themselves.

phrases.english: When he came back,
those residents said to him:
What did you bring to the king's palace?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: מַאי דִּשְׁקַלִי מֵהָכָא אַמְטַאי לְהָתָם.
phrases.english: He said to them: What I took from here, I brought there.
phrases.notes: He is telling the truth, since the dirt did come from their inn. They take it to mean the dirt itself is magic.

phrases.english: They took dirt and brought it there.
They killed those residents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story by showing what happened to the thieves from step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The thieves who tried to profit from the miracle were executed. נחום's trust that it was all for the good was proven right.

steps.title: What was the sin of the Tower builders?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, which says דור הפלגה has no share in עולם הבא, and asks what they actually did wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: The generation of the dispersion has no share in the World to Come, etc. What did they do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and starts a new topic. It asks what sin the Tower builders did, which sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה tells us about the tower and the punishment, but it does not clearly say what the sin was. Since the משנה gives them such a harsh punishment, the גמרא wants to know exactly what they did.

keyTerms.meaning: The generation of the dispersion, the builders of the tower of בבל
Etc.; the rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.english: The generation of the dispersion has no share
in the World to Come, etc.
What did they do?

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוֹר הַפְּלַגָּה אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exact sin did דור הפלגה commit that cost them their share in עולם הבא?

steps.title: דבי רבי שילא: they wanted to break open the sky
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי שילא say the builders planned to climb to the sky and hack it with axes so its waters would pour out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי שילא say: The builders said, 'Let us build a tower and go up to the sky, and hit it with axes so that its waters flow out.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer to the question in step 6. The sin was a plan to attack the sky itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, their sin was not just building something tall. It was a bold plan to break open the heavens. That kind of rebellion explains why their punishment was so severe.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Sheila say:
We will build a tower and go up to the sky,
and we will strike it with axes
so that its waters will flow out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Their sin was planning to climb to the sky and break it open with axes so its waters would pour out.

steps.title: The West laughs: why not build on a mountain?
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of ארץ ישראל make fun of רבי שילא's answer. If the goal was to reach the sky, they should have built on a mountain.
steps.simpleTranslation: They laughed at this in the West and said: If so, let them build it on top of a mountain!
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars of ארץ ישראל attack the answer of step 7. They argue that the builders' actions do not fit the goal of reaching the sky.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says they built in a valley. If they really wanted to reach the sky, a mountain would give them a head start. So the plan to hack the sky does not seem to be the real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: They laughed at it, mocked it

steps.confusionAlert: 'The West' here does not mean Europe or the western world. In the גמרא, מערבא means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

phrases.english: They laughed at it in the West:
If so, let them build on top of a mountain!
phrases.notes: The פסוק says they settled in a valley: בראשית 11:2.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: דבי רבי שילא's explanation that the builders wanted to reach the sky and hack it open.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If they wanted to reach the sky, they would have built on a mountain, not in a valley. So their actions do not match the goal claimed.

steps.title: Three groups of builders, three punishments
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אלעזר says the builders split into three groups with three different plans, and each group got its own punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי ירמיה בר אלעזר says: They split into three groups. One said: Let us go up and live there. One said: Let us go up and serve idols. One said: Let us go up and make war. The group that wanted to live there was scattered by ה׳. The group that wanted to make war became apes, spirits, demons and female demons. About the group that wanted to serve idols, the פסוק says: 'For there ה׳ mixed up the language of the whole earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: Because רבי שילא's answer was mocked, the גמרא gives a new answer to the question of what דור הפלגה did wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer no longer says the goal was simply to reach the sky. It says the builders had three different plans, and it matches each plan to a different punishment. That is how it explains why the תורה's story seems to describe more than one punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops the earlier answer and offers a new one.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yirmeya bar Elazar says:
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the printed גמרא, but some versions leave it out.

phrases.english: They split into three groups.
One said: Let us go up and live there.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת: נַעֲלֶה וְנַעֲבוֹד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: And one said: Let us go up and serve idols.
And one said: Let us go up and make war.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ שֶׁאוֹמֶרֶת נַעֲלֶה וְנֵשֵׁב שָׁם – ״הֱפִיצָם ה׳״,
phrases.english: The group that said 'Let us go up and live there': 'ה׳ scattered them.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 11:9

phrases.english: And the group that said 'Let us go up and make war':
They became apes, spirits, demons and female demons.

phrases.aramaic: וְזוֹ שֶׁאוֹמֶרֶת נַעֲלֶה וְנַעֲבוֹד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה –
phrases.english: And the group that said 'Let us go up and serve idols':

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּי שָׁם בָּלַל ה׳ שְׂפַת כׇּל הָאָרֶץ״.
phrases.english: 'For there ה׳ mixed up the language of the whole earth.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 11:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי שילא's answer after it was mocked in step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was the sin of דור הפלגה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They split into three groups with three wicked plans: to live up there, to serve idols, and to wage war. Each group received a matching punishment.

steps.title: All the builders meant to serve idols
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן says every builder meant to serve עבודה זרה. He proves it by comparing the word 'שם' in the tower story with the word 'שם' in a פסוק about other gods.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי נתן says: All of them meant to serve idols. Here it is written, 'Let us make a name for ourselves.' There it is written, 'Do not mention the name of other gods.' Just as there it means idol worship, here too it means idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא brings רבי נתן, who disagrees with the three groups. He says all the builders had one goal: עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן uses a גזירה שוה. The same word 'שם' (name) shows up in both פסוקים. In שמות it clearly means idols, so in the tower story it must mean idols too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here... and it is written there. This is how a word comparison is set up.
Just as there... so too here. This finishes the comparison.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Natan says:
All of them meant to serve idols.
It is written here: 'Let us make a name for ourselves.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 11:4

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״וְשֵׁם אֱלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים לֹא תַזְכִּירוּ״.
phrases.english: And it is written there: 'Do not mention the name of other gods.'
phrases.notes: שמות 23:13

phrases.english: Just as there it is about idol worship,
so too here it is about idol worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי ירמיה בר אלעזר's three groups and says they all had one goal
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the builders of the tower meant to serve עבודה זרה. This is learned from the word 'שם' through a גזירה שוה.

steps.title: What happened to the tower itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says one third of the tower was burned, one third was swallowed into the ground, and one third is still standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: Of the tower, a third was burned, a third was swallowed up, and a third still stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves from the builders to the tower building itself. רבי יוחנן tells us what became of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds new information that is not in the פסוקים. Only part of the tower was destroyed, and part of it is still standing. That sets up the next statements about the tower's lasting effect.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
Of the tower, a third was burned,
a third was swallowed up, and a third still stands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the builders' sin to the fate of the tower building
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The tower was split in its fate: a third burned, a third swallowed up, a third remaining.

steps.title: The tower's air makes people forget
steps.stepSummary: רב says the air of the tower makes a person forget.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: The air of the tower makes people forget.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds that the tower still has a bad effect today: being near it makes a person forget.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said part of the tower still stands. רב now tells us what that remaining part does. The tower's sin left behind a harmful effect on memory.

phrases.english: Rav says: The air of the tower makes people forget.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the fact that a third of the tower still stands
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The air around the tower causes forgetfulness.

steps.title: בבל and בורסיף are bad for Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the places בבל and בורסיף are a bad sign for Torah learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף says: בבל and בורסיף are a bad sign for Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף continues the idea of forgetting. He names two places near the tower that are bad for Torah learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב spoke about the air of the tower itself. רב יוסף names specific places, בבל and בורסיף, and says they harm a person's Torah.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef says:
Babylonia and Bursif are a bad sign for Torah.
phrases.notes: He means these places make a person forget what he learned, like the tower's air.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of forgetfulness linked to the tower
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בבל and בורסיף are harmful to Torah learning.

steps.title: What does the name בורסיף mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the name בורסיף means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is בורסיף?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the unusual name בורסיף means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple clarifying question, not a challenge. The גמרא wants to know whether the name itself hints at why the place is bad for Torah.

phrases.english: What is Bursif?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in רב יוסף's statement
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the name בורסיף

steps.title: בורסיף means an empty pit
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי explains that בורסיף means 'בור שאפי', an empty pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי says: An empty pit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי answers that the name hints at 'an empty pit'. A place that empties a person of his learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name is read as a play on words. In such a place, a person's Torah drains away and he is left empty. That explains why רב יוסף called it a bad sign for Torah.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi says: An empty pit.
phrases.notes: It is a play on the name: בורסיף sounds like בור שאפי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the name בורסיף
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בורסיף means 'בור שאפי', an empty pit, where a person's learning drains away.
steps.whatToRemember: The section on דור הפלגה ends here. The builders' sin was either three plans (רבי ירמיה בר אלעזר) or all עבודה זרה (רבי נתן). The tower was partly destroyed, and its area causes people to forget Torah.

steps.title: The people of סדום lose עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about אנשי סדום. A ברייתא proves from a פסוק that they have no share in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'The people of סדום have no share in עולם הבא.' The רבנן taught: The people of סדום have no share in עולם הבא, as it says: 'And the people of סדום were wicked and sinners to ה׳, very much.' 'Wicked' means in this world. 'And sinners' means for עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה, about the people of סדום. It brings a ברייתא with a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads two words of the פסוק as two separate ideas. 'רעים' refers to their punishment in this world. 'חטאים' teaches that they also lose עולם הבא.

phrases.aramaic: ״אַנְשֵׁי סְדוֹם אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא וְכוּ׳״.
phrases.english: 'The people of Sodom have no share in the World-to-Come, etc.'
The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: אַנְשֵׁי סְדוֹם אֵין לָהֶן חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
phrases.english: The people of Sodom have no share in the World-to-Come,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאַנְשֵׁי סְדֹם רָעִים וְחַטָּאִים לַה׳ מְאֹד״.
phrases.english: as it says: 'And the people of Sodom were wicked and sinners to ה׳, very much.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 13:13

phrases.english: 'Wicked' means in this world,
'and sinners' means for the World-to-Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַנְשֵׁי סְדוֹם אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה and begins a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people of סדום have no share in עולם הבא, learned from the word 'חטאים' in בראשית 13:13.

steps.title: רב יהודה explains each word of the פסוק about סדום
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains the פסוק about אנשי סדום. 'רעים' means sins of the body, 'חטאים' means sins with money, 'לה׳' means cursing ה׳, and 'מאד' means sinning on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says: 'Wicked' means with their bodies, and 'sinners' means with their money. 'Wicked' is about the body, because יוסף used the word 'רעה' about sinning with אשת פוטיפר. 'Sinners' is about money, because the תורה calls refusing to lend to a poor person a 'חטא'. 'Before ה׳' means they cursed ה׳. 'Very' means they sinned on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה goes word by word through the פסוק 'רעים וחטאים לה׳ מאד' and gives each word its own meaning. He backs up each one with another פסוק that uses the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word in the פסוק is treated as a separate type of sin. רב יהודה links 'רעים' to a body sin, because יוסף called that sin 'רעה'. He links 'חטאים' to a money sin, because the פסוק about not lending to the poor uses 'חטא'. 'מאד' adds that their sins were deliberate, not accidental.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'blessing ה׳', a polite way of saying cursing ה׳
That they do it on purpose

steps.confusionAlert: 'ברכת השם' does not mean they blessed ה׳. It is a respectful way of saying they cursed ה׳.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says:
"Wicked" means with their bodies,
and "sinners" means with their money.
"Wicked" means with their bodies, as it is written:
"And how can I do this great wickedness
and sin against God?"
phrases.notes: בראשית 39:9. This is יוסף refusing אשת פוטיפר.

phrases.english: "And sinners" means with their money, as it is written:
"And it will be a sin in you."
phrases.notes: דברים 15:9

phrases.english: "Before ה׳": this is "blessing" ה׳.
"Very": that they mean to do it and sin on purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: רָעִים בְּגוּפָן, וְחַטָּאִים בְּמָמוֹנָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the words of the פסוק about אנשי סדום that was brought in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In 'רעים וחטאים לה׳ מאד': רעים = body sins, חטאים = money sins, לה׳ = cursing ה׳‎, מאד = sinning on purpose.

steps.title: A ברייתא reverses the meanings and explains 'very' as bloodshed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא switches רב יהודה's meanings: 'רעים' is money sins and 'חטאים' is body sins. It agrees about 'לה׳' and explains 'מאד' as murder.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: 'Wicked' means with their money, because the תורה says 'your eye will be wicked (רעה) against your poor brother'. 'Sinners' means with their bodies, because יוסף said 'and sin (וחטאתי) against God'. 'Before ה׳' means cursing ה׳. 'Very' means bloodshed, because the פסוק says מנשה shed innocent blood 'הרבה מאד'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads the same פסוק in a different way from רב יהודה. It swaps the two main words and gives a new meaning for 'מאד'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the very same two פסוקים, but it pulls a different word out of each one. From the poor-person פסוק it takes 'ורעה', and from יוסף's פסוק it takes 'וחטאתי', so the meanings flip. For 'מאד' it finds the same word in a פסוק about מנשה killing people, so 'מאד' here means murder.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions use the same two פסוקים. The difference is which word each one focuses on from each פסוק.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא:
"Wicked" means with their money,
"and sinners" means with their bodies.
"Wicked" means with their money, as it is written:
"And your eye will be wicked against your poor brother."
phrases.notes: דברים 15:9. This is the same פסוק as before, but now the word 'wicked' is the focus.

phrases.english: "And sinners" means with their bodies, as it is written:
"And sin against God."
"Before ה׳": this is "blessing" ה׳.
"Very": this is bloodshed, as it is said:
"And also innocent blood מנשה shed
in Jerusalem, very much, etc."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 21:16. The shared word 'מאד' connects this פסוק to סדום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same פסוק, flipping רב יהודה's meanings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רעים = money sins, חטאים = body sins, לה׳ = cursing ה׳‎, מאד = murder.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two opinions. רב יהודה: רעים = body, חטאים = money, מאד = on purpose. ברייתא: רעים = money, חטאים = body, מאד = murder. Both agree that לה׳ means cursing ה׳.

steps.title: סדום became arrogant because of the great good ה׳ gave them
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that אנשי סדום became arrogant only because of the huge blessings ה׳ gave them. It describes their wealth using פסוקים from איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: אנשי סדום became arrogant only because of the good that הקדוש ברוך הוא poured onto them. The פסוק describes them: a land that produces bread, with sapphire stones and gold dust, a hidden path that no bird or wild animal ever reached.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא explaining the root cause of סדום's sins: too much wealth made them proud. It proves how rich they were with פסוקים from איוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves from listing סדום's sins to explaining why they sinned. Their land was full of food, precious stones and gold, and it was safe and untouched. That abundance led to arrogance.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a lasting lesson: great blessing can lead a person to pride and sin.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The people of Sodom did not become arrogant
except because of the good
that the Holy One, Blessed be He, poured onto them.
And what is written about them?
"A land out of which comes bread,
phrases.notes: איוב 28:5–8. The גמרא reads these פסוקים as describing סדום.

phrases.english: and underneath it is turned over as if by fire.
Its stones are a place of sapphire,
and it has dust of gold.
A path that no bird of prey knows,
and the falcon's eye has not seen it.
The proud beasts have not walked on it,
nor has the lion passed over it."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַנְשֵׁי סְדוֹם לֹא נִתְגָּאוּ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל טוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the meaning of the words describing סדום's sins to the reason they sinned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סדום's arrogance came from the overflowing good ה׳ gave them.

steps.title: סדום decides to stop all travelers from coming
steps.stepSummary: אנשי סדום reasoned that since they had food and gold, travelers would only take from them. So they decided to wipe out the custom of welcoming guests, as hinted in a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: since our land gives bread and has gold dust, why do we need travelers? They only come to take our money. Let's make the custom of hosting travelers forgotten from our land. The פסוק hints at this: 'forgotten by the foot'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and shows how סדום's wealth turned into cruelty. They decided to keep all travelers out, and the גמרא finds this hinted in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their wealth made them feel they needed nobody, so guests looked like a loss instead of a מצוה‎. 'תורת רגל', the custom of the foot, means the way travelers are treated. The פסוק's words 'הנשכחים מני רגל' ('forgotten by the foot') are read as hinting that they made this custom disappear.

keyTerms.meaning: To make us lose, to take from us
Literally 'the law of the foot': the custom of welcoming travelers

steps.whatToRemember: סדום's great wealth made them arrogant and selfish. They shut out travelers so nobody could share what they had.

phrases.english: They said:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מֵאַחַר שֶׁ״אֶרֶץ מִמֶּנָּה יֵצֵא לָחֶם
phrases.english: Since we have "a land out of which comes bread
and it has dust of gold,"
why do we need travelers?
For they do not come to us
except to take away from us [from our money].
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in square brackets, 'from our money'; others don't.

phrases.english: Come, let us make the custom of travelers forgotten from our land!
As it is said:
"A stream breaks out away from where people live,
phrases.notes: איוב 28:4

phrases.english: forgotten by the foot,
they dried up, they moved away from people."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: וְכִי מֵאַחַר שֶׁ״אֶרֶץ מִמֶּנָּה יֵצֵא לָחֶם וְעַפְרֹת זָהָב לוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, showing what their arrogance led them to do.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of their wealth, סדום decided to end the custom of welcoming travelers.

steps.title: Killing rich people with a leaning wall
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains a פסוק in תהלים as describing how אנשי סדום killed rich people by pushing a leaning wall onto them and then taking their money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does the פסוק mean, "How long will you plot against a man? You will all be killed, like a leaning wall, a shaky fence"? It teaches that they would target rich people. They would sit a rich man next to a leaning wall, push the wall onto him, and then come and take his money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reads a פסוק about a "leaning wall" as a hint to one of the murder-and-robbery tricks of אנשי סדום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about plotting against a man and about a leaning wall. רבא connects the two: the plot was to use a wall that was about to fall anyway, so the death looked like an accident. This adds a concrete example to the earlier steps about their greed and cruelty.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught or explained (a פסוק, usually in a public lecture)
A leaning wall that is about to fall
They set their eyes on, targeted

phrases.english: Rava taught: What is the meaning of that which is written:
"How long will you plot against a man?
phrases.notes: תהלים 62:4

phrases.english: You will all be murdered
like a leaning wall, a tottering fence"?

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיוּ נוֹתְנִין עֵינֵיהֶן בְּבַעֲלֵי מָמוֹן,
phrases.english: This teaches that they would set their sights on property owners,
and they would seat him next to a leaning wall,
and push it onto him,
phrases.notes: They push the wall onto the rich man, so it falls and kills him.

phrases.english: and then come and take his property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues listing the wicked ways of אנשי סדום, now with a specific murder-and-robbery method.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק of the leaning wall hints that אנשי סדום killed rich people by pushing a falling wall onto them and stealing their money.

steps.title: Finding treasure rooms with balsam
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains a פסוק in איוב as describing how אנשי סדום gave rich people balsam to store, then sniffed it out at night to find and dig into their treasure rooms.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does the פסוק mean, "In the dark they dig into houses; by day they seal themselves in; they do not know light"? It teaches that they would target rich people. They would deposit balsam with a rich man, and he would put it in his treasure room. At night they would come and sniff it out like a dog, as the פסוק says, "They return at evening, they howl like a dog, and go around the city." Then they would dig in there and take the money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second trick of אנשי סדום, reading a פסוק about digging into houses in the dark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Balsam has a strong smell. The rich man would store the valuable deposit with his own treasures, and the smell would show the thieves exactly where to dig at night. A second פסוק, about returning in the evening like a dog, supports the "sniffing" part.

keyTerms.meaning: Balsam, a valuable perfume with a strong smell
They deposit (leave something with someone for safekeeping)
Their treasure room, where valuables are stored
They dig through (a wall) to break in

phrases.english: Rava taught: What is the meaning of that which is written:
"In the dark they dig through houses;

phrases.aramaic: יוֹמָם חִתְּמוּ לָמוֹ לֹא יָדְעוּ אוֹר״?
phrases.english: by day they shut themselves up; they know not the light"?
phrases.notes: איוב 24:16

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיוּ נוֹתְנִים עֵינֵיהֶם בְּבַעֲלֵי מָמוֹן,
phrases.english: This teaches that they would set their sights on property owners,
and they would deposit balsam with him,
and they would place it in their treasury.
phrases.notes: "They" here means the rich owners, who put the balsam away with their own valuables.

phrases.english: In the evening they would come and sniff it out like a dog,
as it is stated: "They return at evening; they howl like a dog,
and go round about the city,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 59:7

phrases.english: and they would come and dig through there,
and take that property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רבא, in the same style, giving another trick of אנשי סדום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק of digging in the dark hints that אנשי סדום used balsam's smell to find rich people's treasuries and break in at night.

steps.title: More פסוקים describing their cruelty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists four more פסוקים from איוב that describe cruel behavior, as hints to more of the ways of אנשי סדום.
steps.simpleTranslation: "They spend the night naked without clothing, with no covering in the cold." "They drive away the donkey of orphans; they take the widow's ox as a pledge." "They move boundaries; they steal flocks and graze them." "And he is carried to the grave, and watch is kept over his tomb."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a short list of פסוקים from איוב, without explaining each one, as more hints to the behavior of אנשי סדום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of these פסוקים come from the same chapter of איוב that רבא just used (chapter 24), and the last one is from chapter 21. The list shows victims left without clothes, orphans and widows robbed, and land and flocks stolen. The גמרא leaves the details unexplained, so each פסוק simply adds to the picture of their cruelty.

keyTerms.meaning: They take as a pledge (collateral for a loan)
They move boundary markers (to steal land)
A heap; here, a burial mound over a grave

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא gives no words of explanation here, just a list of פסוקים. Don't look for a missing argument; it is simply adding more examples.

phrases.english: "They lie at night naked without clothing,
and they have no covering in the cold."
phrases.notes: איוב 24:7

phrases.english: "They drive away the donkey of the fatherless;
they take the widow's ox as a pledge."
phrases.notes: איוב 24:3

phrases.english: "They trespass boundaries;
they violently steal flocks and graze them."
phrases.notes: איוב 24:2

phrases.english: "And he is brought to the grave,
and watch is kept over his tomb."
phrases.notes: איוב 21:32

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more פסוקים from the same chapters of איוב to the description of אנשי סדום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: More פסוקים in איוב describe the cruel robbery and abuse practiced by אנשי סדום.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's lecture leads to break-ins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי taught these tricks of סדום in ציפורי, and that same night thieves dug 300 tunnels. The people blamed him, and he answered that he could not have known.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי taught this in ציפורי. That night, 300 break-in tunnels were dug in ציפורי. People came and gave him trouble. They said to him: You gave the thieves a way to steal! He said to them: Did I know that thieves would come?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about what happened when רבי יוסי publicly taught these break-in tricks of אנשי סדום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The thieves of ציפורי learned the break-in methods of סדום from his lecture and used them that very night, digging 300 tunnels. The people blamed רבי יוסי for teaching them. He defends himself: he could not have known that thieves would come and copy what he taught.

keyTerms.meaning: A city in the Galil where רבי יוסי lived and taught
Tunnels or holes dug to break into houses
They were troubling him, giving him grief

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei taught this in Tzippori.
That night there were dug
three hundred tunnels in Tzippori.
They came and were harassing him.
They said to him: You have given thieves a way to steal!
He said to them: Did I know
that thieves would come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells what happened when the teaching about the tricks of סדום was taught in public.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When רבי יוסי taught the tricks of סדום, thieves copied them that night, and he defended himself that he could not have known.

steps.title: The gutters of ציפורי flow with blood
steps.stepSummary: When רבי יוסי died, the gutters of ציפורי overflowed with blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוסי passed away, the gutters of ציפורי flowed with blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the story about רבי יוסי with a miracle that happened in ציפורי when he died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same city that was once dug up by thieves after his lecture showed a strong sign at his death. The gutters running with blood show how greatly his passing affected the city.

keyTerms.meaning: He passed away (literally, his soul rested)

steps.whatToRemember: אנשי סדום used clever tricks, like the leaning wall and the balsam, to rob rich people. When רבי יוסי taught these tricks, thieves copied them; at his death, ציפורי's gutters flowed with blood.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: When Rabbi Yosei died,
the gutters of Tzippori overflowed with blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָא נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story of רבי יוסי in ציפורי with what happened at his death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At רבי יוסי's death, the gutters of ציפורי miraculously flowed with blood.

steps.title: סדום's backward rule for herding the town's oxen
steps.stepSummary: אנשי סדום had a rule: whoever owns one ox herds the town's oxen for one day, and whoever owns none herds for two days.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would say: whoever has one ox herds the town's oxen for one day; whoever has no ox must herd for two days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another example of the wicked ways of אנשי סדום: a rule for taking turns herding the town's cattle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fairness would mean that people who own more oxen do more of the work. Here it is the reverse: the person with nothing, who gets no benefit from the herding, has to work twice as long. This fits the earlier steps, where סדום's 'rules' were really ways to take advantage of the weak.

keyTerms.meaning: herds / shall herd (take the animals out to graze)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as a fair system with a small mistake. The point is that it is deliberately backward: the poor man, who owns no oxen, works the most.

phrases.english: They would say: whoever has one ox
herds for one day,
phrases.notes: He has to herd the whole town's oxen, not just his own.

phrases.english: whoever does not have any, shall herd for two days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the story of רבי יוסי to listing more of the wicked practices of סדום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סדום's herding rule made those with no oxen work twice as long as those who owned one.

steps.title: The orphan who killed the oxen he was given to herd
steps.stepSummary: An orphan, the son of a widow, was given the town's oxen to herd. He took them and killed them, and then he began to speak to the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain orphan, son of a widow. They gave him oxen to herd. He went, took them, and killed them. He said to them:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how an orphan turned the unfair herding rule against the people of סדום. The last words, "he said to them," set up his reply, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The orphan is the weakest kind of person, someone with no oxen, so under their rule he got stuck herding. He killed the oxen, and his explanation is about to follow. It will likely turn סדום's own backward logic against them.

phrases.english: A certain orphan, son of a widow,
they gave him oxen to herd.
He went, took them, and killed them.
He said to them:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a story built on the herding rule from step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An orphan given the town's oxen to herd killed them and then began to answer the people of סדום.
